problem:
The domain of the vector-valued function $f(t)=2{t}^{3}\,i+(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,j+\operatorname{sec}⁡t\,k$ is 

$$
t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),\,t\ne .
$$

What is the missing expression? You may assume that $n$ is an integer.
worked_solution:
To find the domain of $f$, we need the intersection of the domains of the individual components.

- The domain of the 1st component $2{t}^{3}$ is $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

- The domain of the 2nd component $1+\operatorname{cos}⁡t$ is $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

- The domain of the 3rd component $\operatorname{sec}⁡t$ is $t\in (-\infty ,\infty )$, $t\ne \frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi ,$ where $n$ is an integer.

Therefore, the domain of the vector-valued function $f(t)$ is 

$$
t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),\,t\ne \frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi ,
$$

where $n$ is an integer.
